text:
Mari: quick check — we need to pick a sequencing approach for model rollout controls before we lock the Q2 plan. do we prioritize API-first (low friction for devs) or Console-first (safer for enterprise admins)?
Alex: leaning API-first. customers that hit scale want programmatic hooks. lower engineering surface for us to ship and measure.
Sam: +1 for API-first but we should ship a tiny console fallback for visibility (read-only) so support/sales can see state.
Tay: sales perspective — most current leads ask for admin UI because procurement shows up to demos and expects an admin flow. Console helps close deals.
Nora: solutions eng: for on-prem customers console matters a lot. but they’re a small fraction of signups; revenue impact higher for enterprise pipeline.
Mari: trying to quantify with a quick RICE pass so we can be objective. rough numbers, please critique:
```
Feature A: API-first model pinning
  Reach: 6 (monthly active customers impacted)
  Impact: 7 (developer velocity + fewer support tickets)
  Confidence: 6
  Effort: 3 (weeks)
  RICE score ~= (6*7*6)/3 = 84
Feature B: Console-first model pinning (admin UI)
  Reach: 4
  Impact: 8 (enterprise close rate)
  Confidence: 5
  Effort: 5 (weeks)
  RICE score ~= (4*8*5)/5 = 32
```
Alex: that math makes a decent case for API-first. note though effort for API integrability (SDKs, docs, rollout testing) might bump Effort to 4.
Sam: if we add a read-only console view (2 dev weeks) we can reduce churn from sales demos. maybe split work into M1 (API + read-only console) and M2 (full admin).
Tay: that split is pragmatic. commit M1 to GA gating criteria: API endpoints, example SDK, read-only console, and public docs + 2 customer pilot wins.
Nora: add: rollout safety checks (canary, dry-run) are must for enterprise — label as non-blocker for M1 but must be scheduled in M2.
Alex: engineering constraints: we can share backend code for both surfaces. implementing feature flags and canary routing will add infra work but we can defer full policy UI.
Mari: proposed launch criteria for M1:
- API endpoints + stable schema
- SDK sample + quickstart (Doc + snippet)
- Read-only console page showing pin state
- Basic telemetry: who pinned, when, model version history
- 2 pilot customers onboarded
If we hit those, we mark developer UX as shipped and push admin polish to M2.
Sam: operational checklist: add audit logs, KMS tagging, and an easy rollback path. even read-only console should show rollback links to the API docs.
Tay: follow-up ask from sales: include a one-pager we can hand to procurement explaining data access and isolation for pinned models.
Mari: agreed. I'll own the RICE doc and split the ticket set into M1/M2. action items:
- Mari: finalize RICE + PRD (this week)
- Alex: break down infra tasks and estimate (next retro)
- Sam: prototype read-only console mockups (2 days)
- Tay: draft procurement one-pager (end of week)
- Nora: list enterprise safety items for M2
deploy-bot: "deployed branch feature/rollout-surface-split to staging" :rocket:
Alex: thanks — if no objections I'll schedule PM/Eng grooming for Wed and we’ll default to API-first with console-readonly for M1.
Tay: no objections from sales.
Nora: ok from solutions.
Sam: fine from devex.
Mari: OK locking that. will publish in roadmap doc and share with GTM. :white_check_mark:
